olivia: Hi team — hitting intermittent failures when using JSON mode (strict). Sometimes we get "Invalid JSON" parsing errors, other times the response is raw HTML. Repro below.

olivia: curl request that fails sometimes:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```

olivia: response (when it fails):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"choices":[{"text":"{\"answer\": \"Hello\",}\"]}  <-- trailing comma -> parse error
```

maya: thanks — can you paste the raw request headers and an X-Request-ID from one failing run? also which client (node/python/curl) is used when you see the HTML fallback?

olivia: headers from failing request:
- Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...
- Content-Type: application/json
- Response-Format: json
- Strict: true
- User-Agent: my-app/1.2.3
- Accept: */*
X-Request-ID: rq_20240301_83abf

james (sdk): Accept: */* stands out — some proxies or upstreams will serve HTML when Accept prefers */*. If the API does content negotiation and upstream errors, HTML can slip through. Can you try setting Accept: application/json explicitly and re-run? Also which SDK/version?

olivia: repro with node-fetch (failing):
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-live-...',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi', response_format: 'json', strict: true })
})
```
Node fetch default Accept is */* — curl default differs sometimes. I see HTML response in the failing runs (looks like upstream 502 page).

sophie (backend): I pulled the router logs for rq_20240301_83abf — we got a 502 from an upstream content service. The upstream returned an HTML error page (chunked) and some edge logic tried to coerce it. Our JSON strict enforcement should detect non-JSON and return a 502/structured error, but we have a race: when Accept is */* our content-negotiation fallback path served the raw upstream body back to the client in a few bursts. We also saw one case of a malformed JSON body from an internal transformer (trailing comma).

sophie (backend): immediate action: I'll add a router check to reject non-JSON bodies earlier (patching today). For your app: please set Accept: application/json and ensure your client does not auto-inflate or change Content-Type. Also include the X-Request-ID from failing runs so we can correlate.

james (sdk): short-term workaround in SDK: add header "Accept: application/json" by default when response_format=json. We can push a patch to v1.4.2. Also warn customers if strict=true and we detect Accept is broader.

maya: thanks everyone. olivia — can you try the explicit Accept header and report back? if you still hit it, include the failing X-Request-ID and we will follow up with the raw upstream body. I've opened internal ticket #SUP-4921 to track the router fix.

olivia: adding Accept header seems to eliminate the HTML fallback in quick tests. still saw one parse error (trailing comma) — I'll capture X-Request-ID next time it happens. thanks for quick triage! :pray
